title: 3D Chips Push EDA Into New Territory
gist: As AI/HPC chips move to 3D stacking, chiplets, and heterogeneous integration, the hardest problems shift to system boundaries, and customers at Intel, Broadcom, and Qualcomm describe manual exploration, poor interoperability, and late IR/thermal analysis. Incumbents (Cadence, Synopsys, Keysight, Siemens EDA) are layering agentic AI onto trusted, foundry-qualified tools while startups (ChipAgents, Architect Labs, Rise, ITDA, Suitera, Vinci) build AI-native alternatives.

insights.claim: Microsoft's Artour Levin says nearly every AI accelerator now hits a threshold where the hardest problems live at system boundaries rather than inside the chip, while EDA tools were historically built to design chips, not systems.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: System-level co-design tools (package, board, thermal, interconnect) are the growth vector for EDA as AI chips scale out.
insights.quote: They live at the system boundaries
insights.locator: One challenge is that HPC/AI chip design must be considered

insights.claim: Vinci CEO Hardik Kabaria argues the toolchain's model of episodic, end-of-flow physics validation breaks when heat, stress, and electrical behavior span the physical stack, requiring deterministic, solver-accurate physics continuously available across chip, package, board, and system.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: Continuous physics-as-infrastructure is a wedge for startups against incumbent end-of-flow multiphysics signoff tools.
insights.quote: Hardware teams don’t need physics after the design is done changing. They need physics while the design is still moving.
insights.locator: The chip-to-system threshold is where customers are facing challenges

insights.claim: Synopsys' Henry Sheng says vendors should not try to reinvent everything but must reinvent how tools fit together, maintaining coherent data representations and terminology across domains.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: Incumbents' strategy is integration of existing engines, not rewrite, which preserves their installed-base advantage.
insights.quote: If you try to reinvent everything, you won’t do it.
insights.locator: The central question is whether to augment existing EDA tools

insights.claim: Keysight EDA's Nilesh Kamdar says heterogeneity forces floor-planning budgets for loss, signal path, and power delivery to be agreed upfront in 3D designs, leaving very little room for later negotiation.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: Early architectural exploration tools gain importance and budget share in 3D-IC programs.
insights.locator: Heterogeneity puts more pressure on floor-planning challenges

insights.claim: Arteris' Michal Siwinski says 3D and heterogeneous integration technology is roughly 80% to 90% ready for anyone who wants to use it, but is not yet one-size-fits-all because manufacturing and packaging are evolving fast.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: 3D design is broadly accessible but fragmented, sustaining demand for differentiating IP and tools.
insights.locator: Maybe in the future, 3D and heterogeneous design will be out of the box

themes.theme: Customer pain at Intel, Broadcom, Qualcomm

insights.claim: Intel's Lalitha Immaneni recounts a copper-density/warpage concern that took 10 days to analyze and produced unusable output due to poor tool interoperability, and calls for all EDA tools to adopt a CAD-neutral format so customers can mix best-in-class vendors.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: Large customers are pressing for EDA interoperability standards that could weaken single-vendor lock-in and open doors to point-tool startups.
insights.quote: Then I’ve got to bring 10 PhDs in a room [to fix it].
insights.locator: Specific customer challenges

insights.claim: Broadcom distinguished engineer AJ Tufano says HPC chip teams have been 'living in pain' for five or six years, with fundamental architectural changes in custom accelerators every three to six months and a need to match the pace of software as 3.5D complexity rises.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: Custom-accelerator design cadence of 3–6 months creates strong demand for faster EDA and signals intense custom ASIC activity at Broadcom.
insights.quote: We have been living in pain for probably the last five or six years
insights.locator: For now, HPC customers are doing the best they can

insights.claim: Tufano says compute resources for full-chip analysis are stagnant, leaving a gap between early analysis flows that catch gross issues and full IR signoff that happens much too late.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: Mid-flow IR/power-integrity analysis is an unserved niche; tools filling it could win share at hyperscale customers.
insights.quote: then full-blown IR signoff, which happens much too late
insights.locator: There are wins with the challenges

insights.claim: Qualcomm's Venu Sanaka says 3D exploration is largely manual: bump, TSV, and thermal trade-offs are too slow for a roughly one-year design cycle, partitioning analysis must start three to six months earlier, and moving a block between dies in different technologies requires manual 2D floorplanning.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: Early trade-off and partitioning tools for multi-die designs are a clear customer-stated gap and product opportunity.
insights.locator: Others point to similar challenges

insights.claim: Sanaka says multi-chip designs with different technologies make data management and data exchange with internal partners difficult and still immature.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: Design data management across chiplets is an emerging tooling category.
insights.locator: Multi-chip compounds the challenge

insights.claim: Synopsys' Henry Sheng acknowledges current 3D tooling is sub-optimal but says it is acceptable for now because the chips are phenomenally successful, with the industry moving from manual, experience-driven design to automation and from single-domain to cross-domain problems.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: Tool sub-optimality is not blocking AI chip shipments, which tempers urgency for disruptive tool replacement.
insights.quote: These chips are phenomenally successful, so it’s okay for now.
insights.locator: The opportunity to improve tools is large

themes.theme: Incumbents layer agents on trusted tools

insights.claim: Cadence's Vinay Patwardhan says customers with a hundred 2D designers and no 3D designers asked Cadence to build on trusted, foundry-qualified tools, so Cadence made them 3D-aware and now sees the agentic flow as the inflection point for exploration.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: Foundry qualification and designer familiarity are durable moats for incumbent EDA in the 3D transition.
insights.quote: We have a hundred 2D designers. We don’t have any 3D designers
insights.locator: Agentic AI as an additional layer on existing tools

insights.claim: Arteris' Insaf Meliane says AI speeds design-space exploration for 2.5D and 3D-ICs, but AI-generated design decisions must be explainable, traceable, and validated against deterministic EDA engines before signoff.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: Deterministic signoff engines remain mandatory, protecting incumbent franchises even as AI drives exploration.
insights.locator: Others agree that agents offer the extra layer needed

insights.claim: Keysight EDA's 3D tool already analyzes electrical performance at the floor-planning level with what-if material and via-layer changes, with IR drop, power integrity, and thermal analysis to be added soon, and its natural-language agentic layer can be turned off to save tokens.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: Keysight is expanding into 3D architectural multiphysics; token-cost controls indicate customers are sensitive to AI usage costs.
insights.quote: This is not a deep optimization problem. This is an architectural problem.
insights.locator: The latest tools already help with some of the upfront floor-planning

insights.claim: Siemens EDA's Jeff Dyck says agentic autonomous research against benchmark suites, including auto fine-tuning and auto distillation, is working extremely well for building better EDA tools.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: AI is accelerating EDA vendors' own R&D, potentially speeding product cycles and improving margins.
insights.quote: That’s working extremely well for building better tools.
insights.locator: Post-training, continuous learning in agentic AI

insights.claim: ChipAgents' Solaiman Rahim claims its scalable agentic platform, once tuned with a customer's ontology and know-how, could do advanced packaging work in one day instead of months.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: Aggressive time-to-result claims from startups are a disruption risk to incumbents if validated at customers.
insights.quote: you can do your advanced packaging in one day instead of taking months
insights.locator: Agentic AI as the foundation for startup solutions

insights.claim: Startup Architect Labs sits on top of existing flows with specialized agents that let engineers work at the spec/architecture level, pulling in IP such as UCIe interfaces and Arm cores, feeding logic synthesis, and formally verifying as it builds.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: Spec-to-RTL automation shifts value up the stack toward architecture and IP assembly.
insights.quote: We’re elevating you from an RTL engineer to a human architect
insights.locator: Startup Architect Labs puts proprietary, specialized agents

insights.claim: Rise CEO Badru Agarwala says its platform generates high-level models from a spec that run about 30x faster than RTL, can be lowered to RTL via high-level synthesis, and can also go from RTL back to spec to enable hardware/software co-design.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: High-level modeling and HLS could gain relevance as AI generates specs and models before RTL.
insights.locator: Another company developed a two-way AI virtual platform

insights.claim: South Korean startup ITDA offers a no-code, GUI drag-and-drop tool that shifts DFT design left to early RTL and outputs RTL code, SDC, UPF, and DFT tool inputs.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: Shows startup activity in shift-left DFT and power intent, a niche incumbents dominate.
insights.locator: Meanwhile, a South Korean startup

insights.claim: Suitera co-founder Yehea Ismail says the industry faces a crisis only solvable by deep innovation delivering high-accuracy multiphysics simulation much faster, but declined to explain how Suitera achieves its speed beyond saying it took seven years.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: Unverified speed claims warrant skepticism until independently benchmarked.
insights.quote: There is a crisis in the industry, in my opinion
insights.locator: Other companies offer multi-physics simulation tools

insights.claim: Vinci says a 200-case thermal design sweep that took about 16 hours on a legacy workflow now runs in roughly an hour with under a minute of setup, and its physics analysis scales near-linearly beyond 10 billion degrees of freedom.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: Order-of-magnitude thermal-sweep speedups threaten legacy thermal/multiphysics solver vendors.
insights.quote: A 200-case design sweep that used to take about 16 hours on a legacy thermal workflow now runs in roughly an hour
insights.locator: The shift toward physics-based, AI-enabled tools has proof in the numbers

insights.claim: Synopsys' Henry Sheng says incremental 3D/heterogeneous EDA improvements can proceed independently, but non-incremental change requires EDA, design, and manufacturing to move in concert.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: Deep EDA-foundry-customer partnerships become a prerequisite for breakthrough 3D tooling, favoring incumbents with foundry ties.
insights.quote: EDA alone does not optimize what design you can formulate.
insights.locator: From a commercial standpoint, the chip industry consists of EDA, design, and manufacturing

insights.claim: Arteris' Michal Siwinski says that absent new materials enabling bigger wafers, chiplets and 3D packaging are a given and all design must become chiplet-first, multi-die-first, and physically aware including package considerations.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: Structural tailwind for advanced packaging, chiplet interconnect IP, and multi-die EDA.
insights.quote: chiplets are given, 3D packaging is a given, and everything is going to go vertical
insights.locator: For now, the physics are not changing

insights.claim: Siwinski raises the open question of whether logic dies will follow memory into 3D stacking, with 3D logic cubes requiring packaging to evolve further than on the memory side.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: Watch for 3D logic stacking as a next leg of packaging demand beyond HBM-style memory stacks.
insights.quote: will logic dies go the way that memory dies are going?
insights.locator: 3D is an exciting space
